scope: generated fallback outdoor-unit fan face only
reconstructionBasis: Conservative manufacturer-neutral reconstruction of a late-1990s/circa-2000 Japanese balcony condenser fan face. Dimensions below are benchmark assumptions, not a claim about a specific maker/model.

rotor.geometry: five swept/tapered finite-thickness axial blades behind the guard; no opaque disc proxy
rotor.mounting: rotor centered on existing condenser motor/hub axis
rotor.orientation: fan plane parallel to condenser front face; stopped clock angle varies deterministically by unit

wireGuard.geometry: round-section concentric wire rings plus radial spokes; replaces square bar lattice
wireGuard.mounting: front of rotor with positive axial separation

materials.microstructure: subtle injection-molded polymer grain inherited from AC polymer family; no painted highlight
materials.uvAging: mild surface dulling only because rotor is recessed
materials.angularFresnelResponse: broad dielectric edge lift; never metallic

materials.microstructure: subtle aged zinc/steel surface; geometry supplies round-wire highlight
materials.angularFresnelResponse: metallic grazing reflection broadened by aging

weathering.rotor: recess grime and mild UV exposure only
weathering.shroud: UV dulling plus recess dust; rain exposure at outward lip
weathering.guard: rain/UV exposure; ferrous-source aging only, no arbitrary rust

lodPolicy.LOD0: shroud + five-blade rotor + full four-ring/eight-spoke wire guard
lodPolicy.LOD2: shroud + rotor retained; wire guard removed before it aliases
lodPolicy.LOD3: shroud only preserves circular intake silhouette; rotor/guard removed
